name: Disorders of Pentose/Polyol Metabolism

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Disorders of Pentose/Polyol Metabolism

criteria.description: Demonstration of deficiency or dysfunction of enzymes involved in pentose or polyol metabolism (e.g., transaldolase, aldose reductase)
Elevated levels of pentose or polyol pathway metabolites in blood or urine (e.g., ribitol, arabitol, sorbitol)
Presence of characteristic clinical features such as developmental delay, hepatosplenomegaly, and cataracts
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes encoding enzymes of pentose or polyol metabolism
Exclusion of other metabolic or storage disorders with overlapping features

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of enzyme deficiency or dysfunction plus elevated pentose/polyol metabolites and characteristic clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is supportive but not mandatory if biochemical and clinical criteria are met.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Elevated urinary ribitol and arabitol excretion
searchTerms: high levels of sugar alcohols in urine
excess ribitol and arabitol in urine

pathognomonic.notes: Due to polyol accumulation in the lens
Characteristic organomegaly in some enzyme deficiencies
searchTerms: enlarged liver and spleen from enzyme deficiency
liver and spleen swelling related to enzyme problem

common.notes: Variable severity depending on enzyme affected

occasional.notes: Reported in some cases with polyol pathway abnormalities

rare.notes: Dry skin due to metabolic disturbance

laboratory: Elevated pentose and polyol metabolites in urine and blood (e.g., ribitol, arabitol, sorbitol)
imaging: Hepatomegaly and splenomegaly on abdominal ultrasound
Brain MRI may show nonspecific white matter changes
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as TALDO1 (transaldolase deficiency), AKR1B1 (aldose reductase abnormalities)
other: Enzyme activity assays confirming deficient pentose/polyol metabolism enzymes

distinguishingFeatures: Elevated galactose metabolites instead of pentose/polyol metabolites
Early onset liver failure and cataracts
Glycogen accumulation in liver and kidney

redFlags: Early onset cataracts with metabolic abnormalities
Recurrent hypoglycemia episodes unresponsive to standard treatment
